newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to clear Bell for broadcasting.
newsitem.headline: Canada to clear Bell for broadcasting.

text.p: The Canadian government said on Thursday it introduced a bill in parliament that would permit Bell Canada, a unit of BCE Inc, to hold a broadcasting license and compete with cable TV companies.
Industry Canada said the bill amends a 1968 prohibition which prevented Bell from entering the broadcasting business.

Under the amendment, Bell and its Stentor partners will be able to provide broadcasting distribution services once the rules for competition in local telephone services, including tariffs to enable companies and others to launch competitive local telephone services, have been implemented.

"The convergence of technologies means that companies which previously focused on either telecommunications or broadcasting now want to offer integrated services,' said Industry Minister John Manley. "The real winners are consumers, who will ultimately have a coice in who provides their services."

The government announced its intention to amend the Bell Canada Act in August with the release of the Convergence Policy Statement, which cleared the way for cable companies to compete in each other's core businesses.
